font-family: Helvetica; font-size: 12px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: rgb(251, 251, 251); text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">In order to support multi shard mode we need to find a way to shard Postgres (and distribute execution), ideally without making it aware that it is being replicated. Each postgres shard should only talk to a dedicated other shard directly (might be on a different machine) and not to any other replica shards</span>" style="text;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="740" y="120" width="560" height="80" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
The shard client is responsible for managing a SMR interface to a replicated set of servers.
It issues Queries and Commit requests over the network.

Each postgres shard should only talk to a dedicated other shard directly (might be on a different machine) and not to any other replica shards
